scene.description: Face north towards the central domed tower, attached at its base to the Imperial Institute’s long, richly ornamented frontage. Extend connected wings to both sides, with repeated windows, steep gables, chimneys, smaller towers and alternating pale masonry and darker brick bands. A broad carriage road and kerbed pavements occupy the foreground; add sparse horse-drawn traffic and pedestrians in clothing supported by the period photograph. Slender street lamps are visible, but their fuel is not established here. Do not show today’s isolated tower, open lawn around its base or modern campus blocks. Colour guidance: pale Portland stone is supported by the text; brick appears darker in the monochrome images, but its exact hue and the dome’s 1893 patina remain unverified. Use the images for architectural forms, never their sepia cast as material colour.
persists: The central tower’s upper masonry and domed silhouette, allowing for later repair
altered: The tower’s base is integrated into the Institute frontage rather than the later rebuilt freestanding base
notYetBuilt: Modern campus blocks and landscaped space occupying the demolished Institute footprint
gone: The Institute’s connected east and west front wings and smaller end towers
scene.surroundings: North: the tower and connected Institute frontage dominate and block a direct view through to the rear galleries and gardens. East and west: continue the frontage and carriage road laterally; do not replace the wings with open lawn. South: the road and its opposite frontage must be reconstructed from a period plan, still missing from this dossier. The later Royal College of Science building was not yet present; this is not evidence that the entire southern plot was bare. Do not invent specific southern buildings, shop signs or planting. A full 360-degree reconstruction therefore has lower confidence behind the viewer than in the documented forward view.

referenceImages.author: Rijksmuseum (metadata credit); photographer Frith & Co. (object description)
referenceImages.notes: Catalogue range, not an exact 1893 exposure. Frith & Co. is identified in the object description; Artist metadata credits Rijksmuseum. Inspected the downloaded image: tower joined to long wings, alternating light and dark masonry, gables, paved kerbs, horse-drawn delivery vehicle, slender street lamps and a man in a rounded hat. Scaffolding appears at the left end. Do not reproduce card mount, captions, sepia tint or scaffolding as confirmed opening-day detail. Exact bearing unresolved.

referenceImages.title: Imperial Institute south frontage on a postcard mailed in 1903
referenceImages.author: Unknown author
referenceImages.notes: Date interval inferred from the substantially completed tower and the 1903 mailing, not a proven exposure date. The page gives 4 November 1903; handwriting on the face reads 3.11.03. Use for the main facade only, whose general arrangement agrees with the earlier photograph; later additions, temporary awnings and planting are not proof of 1893 conditions. Inspected: raised oblique view, connected wings, central dome, smaller end towers, carriages and pavement. Exclude handwriting, printed title and mount. Exact bearing unresolved.

gaps: The rearward (southern) panorama lacks a verified 1893 plan or photograph. The forward facade is better documented than the full 360-degree scene.

Neither retained image has a securely established 1893 exposure date. The first has a broad catalogue range; the second predates its 1903 mailing. Do not transfer incidental construction or planting details without corroboration.
The exact 1893 dome patina, brick hue, roof covering, road paving material and lamp fuel are unresolved. Sepia and postcard printing do not establish colours.
No verified admission prices or local fares; no verified gallery-attendant uniform. Do not invent them.
Roles describe fictional people supported by documented occupations. The Punch source is satire and must not be treated as a literal eyewitness transcript.

BHO and Imperial live web requests returned 403 in this session; their full previously downloaded text was read locally. Commons metadata was refreshed successfully and both cached images were visually inspected.
No independent subagent audit was run: the human prohibited subagents. A second manual source-to-claim review was performed in the same session.

The two forward-view reference images are ready for a cautious facade trial. Full-era validation remains pending the southern panorama and stronger period-detail evidence; thin_record is an interim research status, not a claim that all archives are exhausted.
